$comment: D-ASM-ARM64-GAS-SPELLS-NO-ROUNDING-MODE-OR-VECTOR-MOVE (P54, lane av) — the rest of the aarch64 scalar floating-point vocabulary, witnessed by EXECUTION. ★★★ THE ONE THAT NEEDED RUNNING: every mnemonic here failed LOUD before this cycle ('unknown mnemonic'), so a build-only arm goes green the moment ANY row exists — including a row bound to the WRONG opcode. `fcvtas`/`fcvtms`/`fcvtns`/`fcvtps` differ from the already-shipped `fcvtzs` in NOTHING but the `rmode` field, so a mis-binding compiles, links, runs, and returns a plausible integer rounded the wrong way. ★★★ THE DISCRIMINATOR IS A HALF, NEVER A VALUE THAT ROUNDS THE SAME WAY UNDER EVERY MODE: at 1.5 all of fcvtns/fcvtas/fcvtps answer 2, so a test on 1.5 would pass under three different instructions. ✔MEASURED on real aarch64 semantics (qemu-aarch64, gcc 13.3.0 AND clang 18.1.3 agreeing on all 43 printed answers), +2.5 gives 2/3/2/3 and -2.5 gives -2/-3/-3/-2, which separates all six pairs; shapes 9-10 assert the disagreements DIRECTLY so four modes folded onto one opcode cannot pass. ★★ THE NaN IS THE ONLY DISCRIMINATOR BETWEEN `fmax` AND `fmaxnm` (shapes 25-28 and 44), which is why one is built out of a bit pattern and carried across the register banks with the cross-file `fmov` — the two agree on every ordinary input. ★ ALL 28 SPELLINGS THIS CYCLE DECLARED EXECUTE HERE; `fmin` was the last without a shape and is 44, numbered out of order so the codes already recorded elsewhere keep their meaning. ★★ THE FMA SQUARE (31-34) pins operand MEANING, the fact easiest to state backwards: fmadd +10, fmsub -2, fnmadd -10, fnmsub +2 for (2,3,4), transcribed from a run rather than recalled. ★ Shape 37-38 read `fcmpe`'s flags through a two-instruction template (`fcmpe` then `cset`), so the signalling compare cannot optimize to nothing. ⚠⚠ NOT ONE SHAPE IS A COPY except the SIMD register move, and that exception is STATED: `mov Vd.16b, Vn.16b` IS a copy, so shapes 39-40 prove it LEGAL and LANE-PRESERVING inside a chain only the vector path can produce, while its BYTES (including the alias's single source reaching BOTH Rn and Rm) are pinned in tests/asm/test_asm_arm64_rounding_dialect_rows.cpp with a wire-deletion mutant. ⚠ `volatile` seeds are load-bearing: the release arm must still reach the templates. ⚠ ARM64 SPECS ONLY — the subject is one dialect's instruction table and one target's encodings. Exit codes name the failing shape; 42 means every shape agreed, which is why the last shape's failure code is 43. ★★ SHAPES 44-45 WERE ADDED 2026-09-02 BY CYCLE P54's LANE `ae` ([[D-ASM-ARRANGEMENT-ERASED-TO-A-WIDTH-BEFORE-ELECTION]]) AND THEY ARE THE ONE PLACE IN THIS FILE WHERE THE TWO REFERENCES DISAGREE: ✔MEASURED, gas 2.42 REFUSES `mov v0.4h, v1.4h` and `mov v0.2s, v1.2s` while clang 18.1.3 assembles both to 0x0EA11C20 — the same word as `.8b`, the ORR alias being bitwise — so one working reference makes them required and DSS was BELOW the union until the lane axis landed. ⚠ EXECUTION CANNOT TELL THE THREE ARRANGEMENTS APART (one word), so what these shapes witness is that the newly-declared vocabulary ASSEMBLES and is LANE-PRESERVING end to end; the discriminating half is the NEGATIVE one — a scalar spelling must not reach a lane form, and a lane width `cnt` does not read must elect nothing — which is a compile-time verdict pinned in `tests/asm/test_asm_arm64_conversion_dialect_rows.cpp`.
